answer: An agent economy trading water from an oasis to farms on a mesa can secure its bridge market with stake-weighted voting: each agent locks tokens for 30 days, and voting power equals its locked stake. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities still yields only 100 tokens of influence. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and bearing token-price risk.
